patch.objective: End services ethically: planned termination, transfer, nonpayment and avoiding abandonment

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Masters content outline: I Values and Ethics, 35% (IB termination of services, including nonpayment and avoiding abandonment); III Intervention and Practice, 32%; the 2026 blueprint in use from 2026-08-03
sources.note: Read in full 2026-11-14 for the course outline (REQ-286).

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (approved 1996, revised 2021): 1.17(b) take reasonable steps to avoid abandoning clients who are still in need of services; 1.17(c) terminate for an overdue balance only if the financial arrangements were made clear, the client does not pose an imminent danger to self or others, and the consequences of nonpayment have been addressed and discussed with the client; 1.02 self-determination
sources.note: Standards 1-3 read in full 2026-11-14 for the course (REQ-286); the wording here is the course's record of them, not a quotation. NASW's Delegate Assembly votes on proposed amendments on 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.

sources.cite: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS), Screen Version (2008): wish to be dead; suicidal thoughts; then method, intent, plan; suicidal behavior
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14. Used here only for the screening questions before a planned ending.

brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker in a small group practice. Daniel Okafor, 41 (a fictional client), has seen you for eight months for depression after his divorce; in April he had passive thoughts of death, which have since gone. He lost his job and his health insurance in August and has paid nothing since. The practice's fee agreement, which he signed at intake, says unpaid balances are discussed in session before any change to services. You have 50 minutes.
